Consult Summary:
- 44-year-old female marathon-in-training with 2-week history of right-sided knee pain and mechanical clicking provoked by running and gym activity; no current swelling or functional loss.
- Advised ice, activity modification, prescribed stronger NSAID, and referred to physiotherapy for full assessment ± imaging; safety-net advice given.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Right knee pain with clicking (2-week duration)
- Onset after increasing run mileage to 7–8 miles while training for June marathon.
- Pain begins ~20 min into run (≈ mile 3); worsened on continued running; leads to stopping.
- Clicking noted during flex/extension while doing abdominal exercises at gym.
- Occasional initial swelling resolved with ice; currently no swelling, redness, instability, locking, or limitation of range of motion.
- Pertinent negatives: no left-knee pain, no giving way, full extension/flexion, stairs/walking unaffected.
- Self-care: ice and ibuprofen 400 mg PRN.
- Clinical impression: likely overuse/soft-tissue injury (rule out meniscal/cartilage or ligament pathology). Planned physiotherapy evaluation; possible imaging if persistent.

Issue 2: Intermittent tingling in right toes post-run
- Single episode lasting “a while” after run; no ongoing numbness, color or temperature change, or calf pain.
- Resolved spontaneously; no current symptoms.
- Differential: transient nerve irritation/compression from swelling or footwear; to monitor.

Issue 3: Occasional lower-leg dependent edema marks
- Noted ankle/sock indentation after prolonged standing; non-persistent, painless; no pitting tested.
- No calf pain, redness, or systemic symptoms.
- Observation only at present.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen 400 mg orally PRN (patient supplied; frequency not documented).
- Naproxen/Aleve (dose/route/frequency not documented; occasional).
- Vitamin D supplement (dose/frequency not documented).
- Melatonin (dose/frequency not documented).
- Alprazolam (Xanax) intermittently for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Cannabis (smoked joint) occasionally.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Hyperopia; status-post LASIK surgery.
- Severe urinary tract infection in past (treated in emergency department).
- Sports bruise to knee months ago (fully recovered).

Social History:
- Lives at 60 Sloane Avenue, London.
- Highly physically active; training for marathon, plays ice hockey.
- Smokes cannabis occasionally.
- Tobacco and alcohol use not documented.
- Employment/living arrangements not documented.

Preventative History:
- No information on cervical screening, mammogram, colon screening, BMD, vaccinations, skin checks, or optometry follow-up beyond LASIK.

Physical Examination:
- No in-consult physical examination performed; no vitals recorded.
- Patient reports full active knee ROM; currently no swelling, erythema, or warmth.

Plan:
- Continue regular ice therapy to right knee.
- Reduce running intensity/distance; stop activity if pain occurs.
- Prescribe stronger oral NSAID (specific agent/dose not documented) to be taken with food; instruct not to combine with ibuprofen.
- Generate referral to physiotherapist for comprehensive knee assessment and rehabilitation plan.
- Consider imaging (e.g., MRI) if physiotherapist or clinician deems necessary based on examination.
- Safety-net: seek urgent medical review if knee develops persistent swelling, redness, heat, systemic fever, or mechanical locking.
- Follow up after physiotherapy assessment or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing expected elements: allergy status, vital signs, formal musculoskeletal exam, medication doses/frequencies, smoking/alcohol history, and comprehensive preventive screening history.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality good; occasional conversational pauses but clinically clear.
